title: Poll workers reportedly protest unpaid stipends at National Elections Commission headquarters
organizer: poll workers; identity and organization unverified
threshold_50_evidence: unknown; no accessible participant estimate or sufficient qualitative crowd description

occurrence_and_date.summary: NEC listing search snippets label an actual poll-worker protest at NEC/HQ January 14, 2021; the listing could not be opened (403), so physical date is withheld pending source access.

participants.summary: Neither search snippet states attendance or provides an adequate crowd description.

demand.summary: Titles/snippet refer to poll workers seeking money or unpaid stipends; event-level demand and whether it targeted state policy remain unverified.

state_response.summary: NEC snippets mention LNP confrontation/arrest and an NEC chair address, without sufficient accessible context to code any response.

notes: Discovery lead only. A Jan14 date, unpaid-payment grievance, police arrest, and official engagement are search-result captions/snippets and not yet read in source context. No attendance inferred from number of poll workers hired, total workforce, or affected staff. Search-only discovery retains null physical date and pending_evidence. A labor demand against the state/public employer is plausible but no original policy demand is established.
open_questions: Did a public gathering physically occur on 2021-01-14, or is that only the listing/publication date?
How many people assembled at one time?
Was the grievance directed at government policy/the state as employer or solely an employer-payment dispute?
What exactly did police do, and did NEC officials receive/negotiate with protesters?
Was this one action or part of a continuous campaign spanning December 2020 and later weeks?

title: Women advocates’ press conference demands protection for Gbarpolu senatorial candidate and supporters
scope: Monrovia press conference concerning the Gbarpolu County senatorial rerun in Nomodatonau
organizer: Coalition of Liberian women advocates and politicians, represented in the report by former Foreign Minister Olubanke King Akerele; candidate Botoe Kanneh also spoke
participants_original: Coalition of women advocates and politicians; no attendance count reported.
threshold_50_evidence: unknown; the article calls it a press conference and identifies a coalition but gives no count of people physically assembled. Group membership and media coverage are not headcounts.

occurrence_and_date.summary: Opened contemporary article reports a Monrovia press conference on Monday, published Tuesday January5, 2021, before the January7 rerun; date Jan4 is derived from the weekday/calendar relation, not stated numerically.

location_and_organizer.summary: Article identifies a coalition of Liberian women advocates/politicians and says the press conference was in Monrovia.

state_target_and_demand.summary: Coalition asked the Government of Liberia to ensure safety for candidate Botoe Kanneh and supporters; Kanneh asked the President and immigration/police authorities to protect voter rights and return seized cards; a speaker called on the Ministry of Internal Affairs to stop traditional interference.

participants.summary: Neither the direct article nor the rights-monitor search snippet reports how many people attended; the number of coalition groups is not a crowd count.

state_response.summary: Search snippet reports a ministerial meeting and assurance; it contains an inconsistent year and describes earlier discussions, so response to this press conference remains unknown.

notes: The gathering is a press conference, not an election rally. Reported demands were state protection, voting rights, return of seized voter cards, and government action against interference; political-process classification is proposed. Because the action supported a specific independent candidate, a reviewer should check whether this is a state-policy demand or partisan election support. Do not infer 50 attendees from the coalition’s membership or the scale of the affected electorate. Prior December electoral violence and detained supporters are context, not responses to this press conference.
open_questions: Was the meeting Monday January4 or another Monday? The numeric day is derived from an article published January5.
How many people physically attended the press conference?
Could an accessible photograph or second report establish at least 50 simultaneous participants?
Is the action best treated as a demand about state electoral/security policy or election-only support for a candidate?
Did the Justice Minister’s reported Jan5 meeting and assurance occur in response to this gathering, or were these prior private discussions?
Was the announced January7 rerun completed without a related public assembly?
